subject: Priority tiger team — routing overrides, mitigation plan & customer readout (CartCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cartco.com
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: EU region spike impacting CartCo — need tiger team and customer comms

Team,

We just got an Ops alert: CartCo (eu-west) is experiencing sustained p95 latency spike and a concurrent throughput drop on our gen endpoints. Summary from the telemetry: p50 is ~230ms (normal), p95 jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.4s over the last 30m; overall successful QPS to CartCo has fallen ~28%. Error rates are low — this looks like tail latency + queueing rather than model failures.

Immediate asks:
- Can SRE confirm root signal (queue buildup, kernel backpressure, or host AVAIL)? Ben, Marcus — can you validate host-level metrics and whether warmstart/KV cache hit rate dropped?
- Product: Soojin, Karthik — are there safe routing fallbacks (lower-latency model variant or quantized profile) we can route CartCo to without >1% semantic regression? We need a rapid risk/benefit check.
- Communications: I will need a short customer readout (2–3 bullets) in the next 30m to send to Alice at CartCo. Draft attached below; please iterate.

Proposed mitigation options (quick picks for discussion):
1) Temporary routing override -> pin CartCo to low-latency variant (v2-lowlat) for next 2 hours.
2) Reserve burst pool (enable dedicated burst capacity) for CartCo to drain queued requests.
3) Apply a soft client-side rate throttle for heavy-chat endpoints and enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for CartCo prefixes.

I’m standing up a short tiger team call — 10:00 AM PT (in 45m) unless we agree to move earlier. If we need to notify Alice now, I will send a brief holding note.

Attachments: cartco_p95_chart.png (p95 trend), bridge_latency_log.txt (last 60m), tiger_team_runbook.pdf (roles & steps).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cartco.com
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: EU region spike impacting CartCo — need tiger team and customer comms

Marissa — I’m on it. Quick notes from infra triage (first 15m):
- Host health: a subset of EU inference hosts showed increased CVM memory pressure coincident with KV cache misses (drop from ~92% -> 57% hit rate).
- Scheduler: we saw batching queues back up for chat-gen endpoints; a small percentage of requests hit the long-path kernel (context > 2k tokens) causing uneven latency amplification.

Immediate actions I can run now (ETA ~12–18m):
- Warmstart: trigger prefix warmstart on the affected host pool to repopulate KV cache.
- Routing override: create a scoped policy that routes CartCo traffic to v2-lowlat (compatible model variant with lower context path) for up to 2 hours. This should reduce p95 but may slightly increase avg token cost.
- Burst pool: allocate reserved burst capacity for CartCo (10% of their steady QPS) to allow draining.

Risks / rollback criteria: if semantic regressions >1.5% on our eval set or error rates increase, we will roll back routing within 15m. Marcus will own rollback toggle.

I’ll post the run commands in the incident channel and start the warmstart now.

—Ben

On Wed, Dec 15, 2027 at 09:14 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, ops@cartco.com
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: EU region spike impacting CartCo — need tiger team and customer comms

Thanks — quick product lens:
- Routing to v2-lowlat is the least-disruptive from an infra perspective. The main question is semantic parity for CartCo’s top-5 prompt families. I can run a 50-request sample compare (automated eval) and get results in ~20m.
- Quantized fallback (int8) would shave latencies but has a higher risk for subtle output changes for generation-heavy templates; I’d use that only as last resort or as a staged canary.

If Ben’s warmstart + routing reduces p95 substantially within 20–30m we can avoid quantization. We’ll prepare a short regression matrix and share before we flip anything irreversible.

Soojin

On Wed, Dec 15, 2027 at 09:47 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> (Ben's triage notes)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@cartco.com>
Cc: CTO <cto@cartco.com>, ops@cartco.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Brief — brief outage/latency spike impacting CartCo (EU) — immediate actions and next steps

Alice —

I’m writing with a quick update and our immediate actions. We’re sorry for the disruption; this is our highest priority right now. Short summary:
- What happened: Starting ~09:00 PT we observed elevated tail latency (p95) impacting CartCo requests in eu-west. This also caused a temporary reduction in steady throughput.
- Immediate actions we’ve taken: warmstart on affected hosts, scoped routing override to a lower-latency model variant for your traffic, and allocated short-term burst capacity to help requests drain.
- Impact: We expect measurable p95 improvement within 20–40 minutes. No customer traffic was dropped; we applied soft rate shaping on the heaviest endpoints to preserve availability.

Next steps / ETA:
- 10:00 PT (in progress): tiger team is executing mitigations (Ben/Marcus leading infra, Soojin/Karthik validating regression).
- 10:30 PT: we’ll share a short readout with before/after p95 charts.
- By 13:00 PT: full verification and either permanent fix or rollback plan.

We will follow up with a detailed post-incident note and if this meets SLA criteria we will initiate the credit process with your procurement contact. I’ll set a 30-minute readout if you’d like to join — suggest 10:45 PT.

Again, apologies — we’re treating this as urgent and will keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Two asks from our side: 1) can you confirm the expected SLA credit timeline and whether we need to open a ticket to start that process? 2) please include a short technical note after the initial remediation (10:30 readout) with the root cause indicators you’re tracking — our CTO would like to be in the loop and is now cc’d.

We’ll hold until your 10:30 readout.

—Alice
Platform Ops, CartCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priority tiger team — routing overrides, mitigation plan & customer readout (CartCo) — wrap and owners

All — quick close-out: we saw p95 drop from ~1.4s -> ~360ms after warmstart + routing override; throughput returned to within 95% of baseline. Soojin’s regression sample showed <0.8% semantic delta on CartCo top-5 templates.

Owners / next actions:
- Ben: keep the routing override in place for 2 hours, own rollback toggle (Marcus backup).
- Soojin: complete a 500-request regression run (due EOD PT) and share the matrix.
- Karthik: validate that billing & quant profiles were not changed; coordinate with Product Billing if any credits need flagging.
- Marissa: send the 10:30 readout to Alice + the post-incident summary and open the SLA credit process in HubSpot.

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination — merging notes into the incident drive now.

—Marissa
